findings.text: the replay decides each row's fired flag with its own settlement skip plus jev_review.claim_contradicts, not through the product's aggregate_docs_review veto path, so '3 of the 46 still fire' is the runner's arithmetic rather than the product's decision. The reader this node repaired, score_docs_review's raw-answer veto scan, is never called by the replay, so a regression there would leave the recorded 3 unmoved. The counts still measure the shipped question (the questions come from jev_review.docs_question_table) and arm b2 imports the settlement predicate rather than re-implementing it, so this is a fidelity gap in the veto route, not in the criterion.

the brief and the done_when state 'at most 3 of the 45 recorded firings' while the replay, the plan comment c-s6-veto-history-landed and the JSON key bar.recorded_total all read 46; the ceiling of 3 is met either way, but a reader comparing the bar statement to the measurement cannot tell whether one row was added or a row dropped.

the arm A row of the results table, and the opening paragraph that summarises it, report arm A recalling 'all 60' planted contradictions, while the JSON records arms.a.passes.1.recall as 59 and arms.a.passes.2.recall as 60; the page's own criterion section then states 59 and 60. The page and the record disagree on one of the two numbers the bar is read from, and the table is the surface a reader takes at face value.
